title: Enterprise Rate Limit & Quota Adjustment — Operational Playbook
author: Rosa Kim
body:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the operational procedures for investigating, mitigating, and permanently resolving customer-impacting rate limit and quota incidents for enterprise accounts. It also documents short-term cost-protection actions we can take on behalf of customers (or for platform health) and the escalation paths for cross-team involvement.

Scope
-----
- Applies to enterprise, dedicated, and private customers where quota/rate-limit events affect availability, throughput, or unexpected billing spikes.
- Excludes self-service free-tier rate-limit automation unless the event escalates to an enterprise impact.
- Covers: token/per-minute throttles, concurrent connection limits, embedding unit quotas, burst policies, and billing protection requests.

Definitions
-----------
- Rate limit: per-customer throughput constraints (requests/minute, tokens/minute, connections).
- Quota: monthly or annual allocation associated with billing commitments (tokens, embedding units, inference-hours).
- Cost protection: temporary measures (throttling, capped billing, emergency credit) to prevent unexpected financial exposure.
- Mitigation owner: CS engineer or SRE assigned to runbook execution.

Monitoring & Alerts
-------------------
Primary signals and alert sources:
- Redwood Console / Alerts: "customer.rate_limit.error_rate > 5% over 5m" and "customer.quota_usage >= 90%".
- Billing pipeline: anomalous daily spend > 3x baseline or > configured alert thresholds.
- Support tickets tagged: "rate-limit" or "quota-spike".
- Customer-provided telemetry via partner integrations (when available).

Dashboards and links (examples):
| Dashboard | Purpose | Owner |
| / | / | / |
| Customer Quota Overview | Live quota consumption by customer and model | Eng SRE |
| Per-tenant Rate Limit Heatmap | Active throttles and 429 spike sources | Serving Runtime |
| Billing Anomaly Feed | Real-time billing spikes > configured thresholds | Finance Ops |

SLOs and Thresholds Table
-------------------------
| Signal | Warning Threshold | Critical Threshold | Initial Action |
| Tokens/min usage | 75% of quota | 90% of quota OR sudden rise > 3x baseline | Notify CS + generate invoice hold? |
| 429 error rate | 1% over 5m | 5% over 5m | Start triage, apply temporary throttles |
| Concurrent connections | 70% of allowed | 95% of allowed | Autoscale/migrate to dedicated pool |

Immediate Triage Steps (0–15 minutes)
-------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge: CS on-call acknowledges ticket/alert in Slack #cs-oncall and sets incident status.
2. Identify customer and tier: confirm customer_id, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), active models and pinned versions.
3. Gather telemetry: attach links to the customer quota dashboard, recent API logs (last 30 minutes), and billing spike report.
4. Assign Mitigation Owner: CS engineer if customer-facing actions required; escalate to SRE if platform-wide.

Triage Checklist (copy into ticket):
- Customer ID: 
- Region: 
- Deployment type: hosted/dedicated/private
- Models in use: 
- First observed: timestamp
- 429 % (5m avg): 
- Tokens/min trend (last 1h): 
- Billing delta (24h): 

Mitigation Playbook (ordered)
----------------------------
A. Short-term customer-protective actions (CS-led)
1. Soft-throttle: apply a short-lived per-key throttle via the Console: set requests/min to 60% of current peak for 15 minutes. Use only with customer consent for non-critical workloads.
2. Temporary quota top-up: for committed enterprise customers, request a one-time quota add via billing ops. Use emergency path (see Appendix). Document with a CHANGE request.
3. Cost cap: enable temporary billing cap for the tenant (blocks further consumption and prevents surprise charges). Requires Finance Ops approval for enterprise with contractual implications.
4. Response template: send initial customer message acknowledging the event, actions taken, and ETA for permanent fix (template in Customer Communications Templates section).

B. Platform/Service mitigations (SRE-led)
1. Autoscale: if the customer is in Dedicated and available GPU pool has spare capacity, trigger migration to a bigger pool using the dedicated migration runbook.
2. Bypass routing: for latency-critical traffic, route to an alternative region or compatible model variant with lower resource usage.
3. Rollback recent model rollouts or configuration changes if the issue correlates with a recent change (check below for rollout correlation queries).

Sequence example (fast path):
1) CS acknowledges and applies soft-throttle (step A1).
2) SRE examines logs; if platform-constrained, SRE scales or migrates (B1).
3) Finance Ops authorizes temporary quota top-up (A2) if customer revenue risk is high.

Escalation Matrix
-----------------
- CS Engineer (level 1): initial mitigation, customer comms. Slack: @cs-oncall. Pager: CS-Pager-1.
- SRE Lead (level 2): platforms mitigations, autoscaling, migrations. Pager: SRE-Pager-1.
- Product / Legal (level 3): contract interpretation for cost protection, emergency credits. Email: enterprise-legal@redwood.ai.
- Executive Escalation: required for outages > 4 hours affecting revenue-critical customers. Contact: Head of CS, Head of SRE.

Customer Communications Templates
--------------------------------
Initial acknowledgement (short):
Hi <Customer Contact>,

We detected elevated rate-limit errors on your account beginning at <time>. We've applied a temporary throttle and started a deeper investigation. We'll update you within 60 minutes with next steps.

- CS team

Initial acknowledgement (detailed):
Hi <Customer Contact>,

Summary: Elevated 429s and unexpected quota usage observed starting <time>.
What we did: applied a short throttle to protect your spend and avoid downstream failures; opened an internal mitigation ticket and requested SRE support.
Next steps: full triage, temporary quota top-up or migration if appropriate, and a post-incident report within 72 hours.

If you prefer us to pause traffic to avoid charges, reply with "PAUSE" and we'll block new requests until you confirm.

Regards,
Redwood Customer Success

Permanent Remediation and Change Requests
-----------------------------------------
- Root cause analysis: collect logs, compare traffic patterns, and test with reproducer prompts.
- Engineering change request (ECR): if the incident was caused by misconfigured default quotas or a model rollout, file ECR with the serving-runtime team. Include reproducible steps and expected rollout backout plan.
- Policy updates: for recurring quota spikes caused by customer integrations, propose updated onboarding checks in Integration Guides (see Related Pages).

Requesting a permanent quota increase (process)
1. CS prepares the quota increase request: justification, expected new quota, billing implications, timeline for change.
2. Submit request to Finance Ops with tagging: "quota-increase: enterprise". Attach usage dashboards and customer PO if available.
3. Finance Ops approves and creates change in billing system. Engineering applies config change and verifies in console.

Rollback and Recovery Steps
-------------------------
1. If a mitigation (throttle/top-up) causes regression, immediately revert the change and notify the customer.
2. Use the serving-runtime rollout dashboard to rollback to the prior model version if a recent rollout correlates with the event.
3. After rollback, run smoke tests with representative prompts and monitor metrics for 30 minutes before marking resolved.

Post-Incident Review and QBR Metrics
-----------------------------------
Required items in the PIR (post-incident review):
- Timeline of detection, mitigation, and resolution with timestamps.
- Root cause and contributing factors.
- Customer impact (minutes of degraded service, error rate, billing exposure in $).
- Action items with owners and deadlines.

Suggested QBR / health-check metrics to include for enterprise customers:
- Monthly quota utilization rate (avg and 95th percentile).
- Number of quota-related incidents in last 90 days.
- Cost-protection actions invoked (count + $ amount protected).
- Average time-to-mitigate for rate-limit events.

Ownership and Contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: Customer Success (Enterprise CS Team).
- Secondary owner: Eng SRE (platform-scale incidents).
- Finance ops contact: finance-ops@redwood.ai.
- Emergency legal: enterprise-legal@redwood.ai.

Appendix: sample CLI/API commands and config snippets
----------------------------------------------------
1) Example: apply soft throttle via admin API (pseudo-CLI)

curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.ai/internal/quota-adjust \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"cust_12345","action":"throttle","requests_per_min":300,"duration_minutes":15,"reason":"temporary-mitigation"}'

2) Example: check recent 429s in logs (query language):

select count(*) from api_logs where customer_id='cust_12345' and status=429 and ts > now() - interval '15 minutes'

3) Billing emergency quota top-up request (email subject template):
Subject: [Quota Top-up Request] cust_12345 — +2M tokens — urgent
Body: customer, justification, expected new monthly quota, PO/contract reference, CS owner, requested effective time.

Change record template (for engineering):
- Change: apply_quota_increase_cust_12345
- Owner: eng-runtime-oncall
- Rollback: revert_quota_cust_12345
- Validation: verify quota reflected in console and ingestion metrics

Postmortem checklist (before closing ticket)
-------------------------------------------
- [ ] Timeline and evidence attached
- [ ] Customer notified of resolution and root cause summary
- [ ] Engineering action item created for permanent fix
- [ ] Review scheduled with customer (if they request) within 7 business days
- [ ] Lessons added to Integration Guide for relevant SDKs if applicable

Last updated by Rosa Kim on 2026-02-14.
